children: Shoe Station reported second-quarter net sales of $284.3 million for the period ended August 1, 2026, down from $306.4 million a year earlier, and second-quarter net income of $6.3 million, or $0.23 per diluted share. Gross profit for the quarter was $90.6 million with a gross margin of 31.9%, and the company lowered its full-year 2026 net sales and adjusted EPS guidance. Shoe Station ended the quarter debt-free with cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $131.6 million.
Net sales: $284.3 million for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026 (compared with $306.4 million in Q2 2025).
Gross profit: $90.6 million for the quarter; gross profit margin of 31.9% (versus 38.8% in Q2 2025).
Operating income: $7.6 million for the quarter.
Net income: $6.3 million, or $0.23 per diluted share, for the quarter (versus $19.2 million, or $0.70 per diluted share, in Q2 2025).
Adjusted diluted EPS guidance for Fiscal 2026 updated to $0.75 to $0.90; GAAP EPS guidance of $0.32 to $0.47.
Comparable store sales declined 7.1% in Q2 2026; Shoe Carnival banner comps down 6.3% and Shoe Station banner comps down 8.5% for the quarter.

Back-to-school (four weeks ended August 29) showed improvement: net sales down 3.3% and comparable store sales down 2.7%, with August comps down low single digits driven by stronger athletic assortments.
Rebanner activity: 20 Shoe Carnival stores rebannered into Shoe Station during Q2 (21 rebanners year‑to‑date); no further rebanners expected in FY26.

Inventory and merchandising: company accelerated liquidation of aged/excess inventory and shifted to more localized assortments for fall; management highlighted a strong boot assortment and incremental fall advertising investment.

Liquidity and capital structure: ended the quarter debt-free with $131.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and completed a $7.0 million purchase of common stock for treasury during the period.
